mechanism_narrative: Stable or slightly rising WORKPLACES mobility sustains commuting and lunch-trip circulation, which lifts nearby retail visits within four weeks. If workplace mobility stops improving, the retail effect weakens and RETAIL_REC should not rise further.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed positive around 4-5% while TRANSIT stayed near zero across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains at or above its current level for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility is elevated, people substitute toward local shopping and short discretionary outings, so retail-and-recreation rises over the next one to two weeks. If residential time does not remain above baseline, the impulse fades quickly.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 3% week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL remains above 3% for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates broader mobility normalization, which expands access to malls, restaurants, and entertainment venues and pushes RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks. If only one of the two series improves, the retail response is smaller and may not materialize.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to outperform its prior four-week mean over the next 28 days despite simultaneous increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops sharply, access friction rises and discretionary retail trips fall within one week. This mechanism is strongest when the transit drop is abrupt enough to signal restriction or service disruption rather than normal noise.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below 0 and declines by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after TRANSIT crosses below 0 and loses more than 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays unusually high while PARKS remain weak, household spending shifts toward essentials and away from leisure retail, so RETAIL_REC is flat to lower over the next two weeks. The effect should disappear if park visits rebound strongly.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above 40% and PARKS remain below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility signals more leisure-oriented out-of-home activity, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation spending with about a four-week lag. If park usage stalls or reverses, the retail lift should not persist.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days when PARKS improve for at least two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both weaken together, weekday trip chains compress and retail footfall falls over the following month. The effect requires both proxies to move down, because isolated changes in only one series do not reduce total trip generation enough.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES turns negative or falls by at least 2 points while TRANSIT also falls below its prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after simultaneous weakening in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a small but persistent rise in TRANSIT above zero acts as an early access channel for discretionary shopping, and RETAIL_REC should edge higher within two weeks. If transit remains flat near zero, the retail signal should be weak or absent.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above 1 and stays there for 2 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after TRANSIT stays above 1 for two consecutive weeks.
